To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a heterogeneous disease; (ii) the molecular characterization of TNBC is essential for the development of new targeted therapies; (iii) the identification of TNBC subtypes is essential for the identification of patients that could benefit from targeted therapies; and (iv) TNBC is associated with worse prognosis.
triple-negative breast cancer patients with high levels of the immune markers PD-L1 and CD68, as well as high tumor cell proliferation, have poor prognosis.

the expression of the immunohistochemical (IHC) markers estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), and HER2 are associated with the molecular subtypes of breast cancer, that ER, PR, and HER2 are prognostic factors in breast cancer and that the IHC markers are used in the clinical practice of breast cancer to guide treatment decisions.

the development of a novel approach for the detection of breast cancer in the early stages of the disease, which is based on a combination of immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence.
the development of a new class of immunohistochemistry markers for triple negative breast cancer.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no conclusive evidence that triple negative tumors are more aggressive than ER/PR positive tumors, but they are likely more aggressive than ER and PR negative tumors.
there is no single biomarker or biomarker panel that can be used to diagnose triple negative breast carcinoma.
the triple negative phenotype is a heterogeneous group of tumors that share a similar clinical outcome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the immunohistochemical profile for triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) is more heterogeneous than initially thought and that there is no single immunohistochemical marker that can replace the current clinical definition of this subtype.

our data show that the immunophenotypic characteristics of triple negative breast carcinoma (TNBC) are heterogeneous and do not correlate with the expression of estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), or human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2), nor with the presence of a basal phenotype.
the immunohistochemistry (IHC) markers that are most commonly used to classify breast carcinomas are not always concordant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a new biomarker for triple negative breast cancers.

we found the expression of a set of genes in triple negative breast cancer (TNBC), including genes involved in cell cycle regulation, cell proliferation, and cell death, to be associated with the expression of the immune checkpoint PD-L1 and with the presence of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) and with the presence in the tumor of immune cells.
the triple-negative phenotype is not a homogeneous group of tumors.
